title: Olin / Huntsman Model Review & Investment Banking Flashcards
description: Four rebuilt decks: 400 contextual model-review cards, 160 cards from the July 28 equity and Sources & Uses build, 400 source-derived M&I cards preserved from the prior app, and 400 applied technical-interview cards. Includes the existing FSRS-style scheduler.

model_status.estimated_completion: Both standalone three-statement models and Sources & Uses are substantially complete. PPA / Goodwill is next.
next_focus: Build PPA / Goodwill from consideration and closing target balances.
Build incremental PP&E depreciation and identifiable-intangible amortization.
Build Synergies & Integration and the Pro Forma Opening Balance Sheet.
Build consolidated three statements, accretion / dilution, credit metrics, sensitivities, and checks.

usage_note: The 400 M&I Real cards are preserved from the prior app. Every other deck was rewritten into concise, workbook-specific or applied interview scenarios with plausible near-miss distractors. Custom questions and options were length-limited so the app can display them in full.

questions.question: You open the workbook and see that the forecast balance-sheet check is off by $12mm after a schedule change. Which treatment is correct?
options: Trace the missing, duplicated, or mislinked account; do not plug cash or equity.
Increase cash by $12mm so Assets equal Liabilities plus Equity.
Reduce retained earnings by $12mm because equity is the natural balancing account.
Round every balance-sheet line to whole millions and ignore the residual.
questions.explanation: A balance-sheet plug hides the error. The check exists to identify broken accounting or linkage logic.
questions.source_basis: Olin/Huntsman workbook mechanics and July 25-28 checkpoints

questions.question: You open the workbook and see that the assumptions page calculates debt balances directly while a separate debt schedule also calculates them. Which treatment is correct?
options: Make the assumptions page the source of truth because it is the first tab reviewers see.
Average the two debt calculations so neither schedule dominates.
Make the debt schedule the source of truth and link only summarized outputs to the assumptions page.
Keep both calculations and use whichever one gives the cleaner result.
questions.explanation: Detailed schedules should own mechanics; summary pages should display linked outputs to avoid conflicting logic.
questions.source_basis: Olin/Huntsman workbook mechanics and July 25-28 checkpoints

questions.question: You open the workbook and see that historical debt comes from reported statements but forecast debt is driven by tranche roll-forwards. Which treatment is correct?
options: Use historical statements as the source for actuals and the debt schedule as the source for forecast periods.
Use the debt schedule for both actuals and forecasts even when it does not reconcile to reported history.
Use the historical raw debt row for every forecast year to avoid circularity.
Hardcode the first forecast year and let later years roll from it.
questions.explanation: The source of truth changes at the forecast boundary: reported actuals for history, supporting schedules for projections.
questions.source_basis: Olin/Huntsman workbook mechanics and July 25-28 checkpoints

questions.question: You open the workbook and see that depreciation is already embedded in COGS and operating expenses, but the model also has a D&A schedule. Which treatment is correct?
options: Add D&A as a separate operating expense and leave COGS unchanged.
Use the schedule for the PP&E roll-forward, EBITDA memo, and CFO add-back without adding a second operating expense.
Remove depreciation from the cash flow statement because it is already in COGS.
Treat the D&A schedule only as a formatting memo with no balance-sheet impact.
questions.explanation: Adding D&A again on the income statement would double count expense.
questions.source_basis: Olin/Huntsman workbook mechanics and July 25-28 checkpoints

questions.question: You open the workbook and see that depreciation increases by $10 with a 25% tax rate and no other changes. Which treatment is correct?
options: Operating income falls $10, net income falls $10, CFO is unchanged, and cash is unchanged.
Net income falls $7.5, CFO rises $10, and total assets stay unchanged.
Operating income falls $10, net income falls $7.5, CFO rises $2.5, net PP&E falls $10, cash rises $2.5, and retained earnings falls $7.5.
Operating income is unchanged because depreciation is noncash; only net PP&E falls $10.
questions.explanation: The tax shield offsets part of the earnings decline; cash rises only by the tax benefit.
questions.source_basis: Olin/Huntsman workbook mechanics and July 25-28 checkpoints
